AGENDA
  SPECIAL MEETING: GLENDALE CITY COUNCIL
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) MUNICIPAL SERVICES BUILDING
  633 E. Broadway, Room 105 (MSB 105)
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Welcome to Glendale City Hall. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and
 rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the
 proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings are also archived on the
 City Website for viewing anytime at http://www.glendaleca.gov/government/agendas-minutes . If you
 have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City
 Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who wish
 to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City Clerk’s
 office at 818-548- 2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify the language
 for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not required and
 persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  APRIL 13, 2020

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale City Council meeting will be available to the public
electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

MINUTES
  SPECIAL MEETING: GLENDALE CITY COUNCIL
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) MUNICIPAL SERVICES BUILDING
  633 E. Broadway, Room 105 (MSB 105)
  Glendale, CA 91206
  APRIL 13, 2020

 The Special Meeting of the Glendale City Council convened in the Municipal Services Building,
 Room 105, in said City, at 6:00 p.m. on the above date, pursuant to a call for such meeting
 signed by the City Clerk of the City Council, and on file with the City Clerk, a copy of which is as
 follows:
  April 8, 2020
  Date

A SPECIAL PUBLIC MEETING of the City Council is hereby called to meet at 6:00
p.m. on Monday, April 13, 2020, in the Municipal Services Building, 633 E. Broadway, Room
105 (MSB 105), Glendale, CA 91206 to consider the following item(s) of business, to wit;
  1. Comments by Mayor Najarian
  2. Selection of a New Mayor
  3. Comments by New Mayor

Written Notice of said meeting was given, which Notice consisted of a copy of the
foregoing Call, and was served on each Member of the Council not joining in the Call, and
upon the in said City not less than 24 hours before the time fixed in said Call for said
meeting, as follows:
Upon Vrej Agajanian  at 5:00 p.m.  April 8, 2020  Glendale, CA
Upon Dan Brotman  at 5:00 p.m.  April 8, 2020  Glendale, CA
Upon Ardy Kassakhian  at 5:00 p.m.  April 8, 2020  Glendale, CA
Upon Paula Devine  at 5:00 p.m.  April 8, 2020  Glendale, CA
Upon Ara Najarian  at 5:00 p.m.  April 8, 2020  Glendale, CA
 Mayor Najarian called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL –  All Present
  -  Report of the City Clerk of the City Council, re: Posting of Agenda. The
  Agenda for the Monday, April 13, 2020 Special Public Meeting of the City
  Council was posted on Wednesday, April 8, 2020 on the Bulletin Board
  Outside City Hall.

  1. Comments by Mayor Najarian
  Mayor Najarian thanked the Council Members both new and old, who have supported
  him and the City during this last year. He thanked all city staff who helped him and the
  Council in governing the City to move forward. It was a very busy year, from losing
  Council Member Sinanyan to appointment of Council Member Quintero.

  He was able to accomplish several things during his tenure: approval of the Integrated
  Resource Plan; approval of the revised plan to repower Grayson Power Plant;
  participation of Eland 1 Solar Energy project; approval of the contract with SCAPPA
  (Southern California Public Power Authority) for renewable geothermal energy; approval
  of the Lobbyist Registration Ordinance; a productive meeting with the Board of Trustees

  4A
  04 13 20

   of the Glendale Community College; assessment program and prioritization of street
  pavement by Public Works; Cities Non-profit Summit; grand-opening of Vista Garden for
  senior housing; approval of rent subsidy program; purchased two large properties for
  affordable housing; obtained electric battery-operated leaf blowers, lawnmowers,
  hedgers, and trimmers; turned park locations into green zones; approval of the Bus
  Rapid Transit project from Metro; received grant funds for CicLAvia; approval of the
  Microtransit Pilot Program by Metro; completion of the Beeline Maintenance Facility;
  increased in number of green fleet vehicles; unveiled of new electric bus by BYD
  Manufacturing; completion of planning by Metrolink Rail System; feasibility study of
  street cars; and received grant funds for safety crosswalks in the Pelancony area.

  He wanted to work on the following but has not yet come to fruition: Election reform;
  provide financial assistance to Glendale Unified School District regarding construction of
  a high school swimming pool; continuation of the Fremont Park Renovation Project; his
  trip to Japan to restore relationship with Sister City Higashiosaka; and establish the
  Mexican Sister City Program.

  Mr. Najarian indicated that the best news he has received during his tenure as Mayor
  was when the City won the lawsuit regarding the transfer of GWP funds to the General
  Fund. He thanked the City Attorney Mike Garcia for his evaluation and analysis of the
  legal principles of the case. The continued transfer of funds was deemed to be legal and
  permissible based on the City’s Charter.

  Lastly, he will very much relish going back to his role as a Council Member. Based from
  his observation, he gets more work done as a Council Member than being a Mayor. He
  thanked everyone for a great term and wished his very best to the new Mayor.

2. Selection of a New Mayor
  Acting City Clerk Aram Adjemian asked Council for nomination of Mayor. Najarian
  nominated Agajanian for the Office of the Mayor. Seconded by Devine. No other
  nominations were called.
  Vote as Follows
  Ayes:  Agajanian, Brotman, Devine, Kassakhian, Najarian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  None

  Councilmember Agajanian is declared as the next Mayor of Glendale for the ensuing
  year.

3. Comments by New Mayor
  Mayor Agajanian thanked Council, city staff, and residents of Glendale for their support
  and entrusting him to the position of Mayor. He is humbled and promised to do his best
  especially during the unprecedented crisis we are all experiencing. He also thanked
  outgoing Mayor Najarian for his leadership and service to the City of Glendale.

  His goal during his tenure: aggressively support programs for affordable housing
  opportunities; ensure neighborhoods are good places to live; continue to invest in
  infrastructure to improve streets and community centers, preserve the rich history and

  04 13 20
  SP CC
   cultural offerings of the city; and balance the need to make sound sustainable decision
  while providing reliable services – balance innovation and reliability, sustainability, and
  efficiency.

  Mr. Agajanian grew up in poverty and saw the value of hard work and education. Later,
  he became a California Certified Professional Engineer. Helping people has been his
  lifelong passion and has been involved in several nonprofit organizations. He currently
  owns two TV stations that broadcast in Southern California through local cable and via
  online. He is also a host of a show that runs every night, which educate the viewers of
  facts and figures regarding US government, social, and political issues. He was elected
  by the Glendale residents as a Council Member to be their voice and does not represent
  any special interest groups.

  The COVID-19 pandemic has caused so much hardship in our lives and must be dealt
  with compassion, hope, honesty, and leadership. He is ready tackle on the
  responsibilities and challenges with the help of Council. Like the enemies of the past, we
  will be victorious and emerge stronger bonds, clear minds, and renewed spirits.

ADJOURNMENT – 6:51 p.m.
  Moved: Devine  Seconded: Kassakhian

  Mayor of the City of Glendale

  City Clerk of the City of Glendale
